title: Two distinct lines meet in at most one point, in any incidence structure
statement: In any incidence structure -- any inhabitant of the record Geo.Incidence, not any particular plane -- two lines that are not equal cannot both carry two points that are apart. Stated contrapositively, which is the form this kernel can express without subtracting points: given lines l and m, points P and Q that are apart, and all four incidences (P and Q each on both l and m), the assumption that l and m are unequal is refuted. This is the classical 'two distinct lines meet in at most one point' and it is a THEOREM about the axioms rather than a fact about coordinates: its proof is the uniqueness half of Hilbert I.1 applied to the four incidences, and nothing else. The distinctness of the two points is an apartness in the structure's own sense, not the negation of point equality, which is what lets one statement serve a model over the rationals and a model over the reals.

formal.statement: theorem Geo.Incidence.distinct_lines_meet_once : ((x0 : Geo.Incidence) -> ((x1 : Geo.Incidence.point x0) -> ((x2 : Geo.Incidence.point x0) -> ((x3 : Geo.Incidence.line x0) -> ((x4 : Geo.Incidence.line x0) -> ((x5 : ((x5 : Geo.Incidence.lEq x0 x3 x4) -> False)) -> ((x6 : Geo.Incidence.apart x0 x1 x2) -> ((x7 : Geo.Incidence.on x0 x1 x3) -> ((x8 : Geo.Incidence.on x0 x2 x3) -> ((x9 : Geo.Incidence.on x0 x1 x4) -> ((x10 : Geo.Incidence.on x0 x2 x4) -> False)))))))))))

notes: The contrapositive form is not a weakening for convenience, it is what the kernel can say. The direct form -- 'if l and m are distinct then any two points on both are equal' -- would need to CONCLUDE a point equality, and the structure's point equality is an abstract setoid relation whose only introduction rules are its own reflexivity and the congruence fields; there is nothing to conclude it FROM. The contrapositive consumes an apartness instead, which the structure does supply. This is the same shape the rest of this kernel's constructive statements take, and the reason `Geo.Incidence` carries an apartness field at all is recorded in ADR-1635.
